summary:
Space Graveyard is an educational website that explores the stories of NASA hardware left on the Moon and Mars. Through artifact profiles, fictional letters, and interactive learning activities, the project introduces young space enthusiasts to machines such as the Apollo Lunar Module Descent Stage, Surveyor landers, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and Viking 1.

The website addresses the challenge by turning NASA mission history into engaging and easy-to-understand stories that explain what each machine was designed to do, what scientists learned from it, and what happened after its mission. The website also has an interactive map where users can click on a mission and learn about it.

This project is important because space exploration does not end when a mission is over. By preserving the stories and discoveries of these machines, Space Graveyard helps people appreciate the science, engineering, and exploration that continue to shape our understanding of the Moon and Mars.
details:
Space Graveyard is an educational website designed to help young space enthusiasts discover the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars. The website works like a virtual space museum by allowing visitors to explore different artifacts, learn about the missions they belonged to, and understand the scientific discoveries they helped make possible.

The project features separate Moon and Mars sections, a “Letters from Space” section and an interactive explore section. The letters use fictional first-person storytelling to give each piece of equipment a voice and help visitors imagine its journey, while the accompanying facts explain the real mission history and discoveries.

The project also features an interactive map where users can click on the buttons and explore the artifacts in Moon and Mars. I used HTML to code this page.

The goal is to make space science more interesting and accessible to younger audiences. By connecting scientific information with storytelling, SPACE GRAVEYARD encourages curiosity about space exploration, engineering, and the lasting impact of NASA missions.

I developed the project using Wix, including its website editor and design tools. I used a web browser to research NASA missions and verify information using NASA resources.

The creative aspect of the project is its virtual museum concept and its use of fictional letters to tell the stories of real machines. I chose a dark, futuristic space-inspired design to make the website feel like an exploration archive. Important factors I considered included scientific accuracy, age-appropriate explanations, easy navigation, and visual appeal.
